tips.q: What prompt restores old photos without changing the face?
tips.a: Use `restore this old photo to modern clarity, preserve original identity, facial structure, and proportions exactly`. Avoid words like `modernize the face` or `beautify` alone — they push the model toward a generic AI look instead of your real ancestor.

tips.q: Can ChatGPT restore and colorize old photos?
tips.a: Yes — GPT Image 2 (the image model behind ChatGPT) handles both in one pass. Add `colorize naturally with realistic skin tones, era-accurate colors for [decade]` to your restore prompt. It works best for 1900s-1980s photos with clear lighting cues.

tips.q: How do I preserve identity in AI photo restoration?
tips.a: Three rules: (1) upload the highest-resolution scan you have, no phone-of-photo glare; (2) include `preserve facial features, hairstyle, and proportions exactly`; (3) skip stylization words like `cinematic` or `anime` that override likeness.

tips.q: What should I avoid when restoring old family photos with AI?
tips.a: Avoid generic prompts like `make this beautiful`, heavy stylization tags (`HDR`, `dramatic`), and over-aggressive upscaling on already-blurry scans. Also skip `young again` modifiers — they invent a face that never existed instead of restoring the real one.

faq.q: What's the best prompt to restore old photos with GPT Image 2?
faq.a: Start with: 'Restore this old photo to modern professional quality. Preserve facial features, hairstyle, and clothing exactly. Remove scratches, dust, fading, and color casts. Output ultra-high clarity with realistic skin tones and natural lighting.' Then layer in colorize / period-accurate / upscale modifiers depending on the source.

faq.q: How do I keep the face looking like the original person?
faq.a: Always include 'preserve original identity, facial structure, and proportions' in your prompt. Avoid words like 'modernize' alone — pair them with 'while keeping likeness exact'. Upload at the highest resolution scan you have (avoid camera-of-photo glare).

faq.q: GPT Image 2 vs Gemini Nano Banana for photo restoration — which is better?
faq.a: GPT Image 2 wins on detail preservation and skin texture realism. Gemini wins on speed and free tier availability. For high-stakes family photos use GPT Image 2; for quick previews use Gemini. Many users compare both — see our side-by-side test.

faq.q: Can GPT Image 2 colorize black-and-white photos?
faq.a: Yes — it does period-accurate colorization based on era cues (clothing, lighting, decade). Add 'colorize naturally with realistic skin tones, era-accurate colors for [decade]' to your prompt. Works best for 1900s-1980s photos.

faq.q: Do I need a paid plan to restore photos?
faq.a: GPT Image 2 Studio offers free starter credits (1K resolution restore = 6 credits per attempt). One restored photo typically takes 1-2 generations to dial in. For high-volume archival projects, see our pricing — credits scale economically vs paid services like VanceAI or MyHeritage.
